newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish shares end lower as Astra tumbles on result.
newsitem.headline: Swedish shares end lower as Astra tumbles on result.

text.p: Swedish shares ended lower on Monday after a dull day's trade with drugs company Astra dragging the market lower on a weak first quarter result in late afternoon trade.
The Stockholm general index fell 0.62 percent to 2,634.85 as shares worth 3.56 billion crowns changed hands.

Most losses were posted after drugs major Astra posted a weaker-than-expected pre-tax profit for the first quarter of 1997. Astra plunged 22 crowns to 320.5 after reporting a pre-tax profit of 3.46 billion crowns against market expectations of a profit of 3.93 billion crowns.
The drug sector index fell 5.15 percent.
"Astra's report was not really so bad as to deserve this market reaction," said Ingemar Kihlstrom, Aros analyst. "Sales were a bit worse than expected but not dramatically.
"In the longterm Astra is a good buy."
The company said stockpiling prior to the end of 1996 wiped about 400 million crowns off first quarter sales.
Handelsbanken ended five higher at 226 after posting a 14 percent higher first quarter profit after credit losses of 1.73 billion crowns against expectations of 1.64 billion crowns.
Market heavyweight telecoms group Ericsson rose one to 251 crowns.
